asset.title: Build the Machine, Not the Ad

ranked_reasons.finding: The asset ends on the author's job, not the reader's — it asks for reach instead of delivering the reader's next progress.
ranked_reasons.evidence: Follow False Dawn Industries to get each one the day it drops.

ranked_reasons.finding: The emotional/social layer of the job is unspoken. The subtitle names a CMO, but the body never names the fear driving them (career exposure when the reach bet fails).
ranked_reasons.evidence: For thirty years, marketing has been a bet on reach... That bet is over.

ranked_reasons.finding: Audience drifts from the named CMO to a generic 'you' mid-article, diluting the defined circumstance.

rewrites.original: Follow False Dawn Industries to get each one the day it drops, and pressure-test the thinking against real, working code at github.com/jratlee/FDI.
rewrites.revised: Before your next budget cycle, pick one marketing asset you could prove you own — a corpus, an identity, an interface an agent could call — and audit whether you actually own it. If you can't name one, that's your Q1. The working code and the next Field Guides are at github.com/jratlee/FDI.
rewrites.rationale: progress delivered — converts an author-serving reach ask into a concrete first action the reader takes Monday.

rewrites.original: That bet is over, and most 2026 budgets haven't noticed yet.
rewrites.revised: That bet is over, and the CMO who renews it in 2026 is the one who has to explain the miss when it doesn't compound.
rewrites.rationale: job clarity (emotional/social) — names the career stakes, not just the market fact.

ranked_reasons.finding: The economic case is macro, not tied to a driver on the reader's own P&L. A CFO discounts industry totals; connect it to CAC, retention/LTV, or capital efficiency the reader controls.
ranked_reasons.evidence: The world will spend $1.3 trillion on advertising in 2026.

ranked_reasons.finding: Load-bearing stats are asserted, not sourced, which weakens the claim in a boardroom.
ranked_reasons.evidence: the average digital ad earns about 2.5 seconds of active attention.

ranked_reasons.finding: Strength — category authority is genuinely differentiated and code-backed (Pile, Talk to NYC). Keep this; it is the asset's moat.

rewrites.original: Every quarter you spend buying commoditized reach is a quarter you didn't spend building the identity, the corpus, and the interfaces...
rewrites.revised: Every quarter you spend buying commoditized reach raises the CAC you can't lower and builds no asset you keep — while a corpus, an identity, and an agent-callable interface compound into retention you own.
rewrites.rationale: value-driver linkage — re-anchors the claim to CAC and retention, drivers a CFO already tracks.

gates.framework: GEO/AEO (Aggarwal et al., KDD 2024) + Google E-E-A-T + Schema.org

ranked_reasons.finding: The thesis is not extractable: an answer engine that lands here can't lift a single attributable sentence that states the claim, because it sits at paragraph 8.
ranked_reasons.evidence: when reach is commoditized and platforms are opaque, the only durable marketing assets are the ones you own and can prove.

ranked_reasons.finding: Citable numbers carry no citation, so no engine will attribute them to you (the GEO-proven lever is cited statistics).
Strength — human-signal density is excellent: named thinkers, a dated thesis, two real shipped builds. This is what a model can't fabricate.

rewrites.original: The cost of making content just fell to zero. That's not the opportunity. That's the emergency.
rewrites.revised: The cost of making content just fell to zero. That's not the opportunity — it's the emergency. When reach is commoditized and ad platforms are opaque, the only durable marketing assets are the ones you own and can prove.
rewrites.rationale: answer-engine structure — front-loads the extractable, attributable thesis into the opening so a generative engine can quote it.

rewrites.original: The world will spend $1.3 trillion on advertising in 2026, and the average digital ad earns about 2.5 seconds of active attention.
rewrites.revised: Global ad spend is forecast to pass $1.3 trillion in 2026 (WARC), while eye-tracking studies put active attention on the average digital ad at roughly 2.5 seconds (Ebiquity / Amplified Intelligence).
rewrites.rationale: answer-engine structure + metadata — cited statistics are the GEO-proven lever for being quoted as a source; also fixes Gate 2 substantiation.

top_moves.move: Replace the closing 'Follow False Dawn Industries' CTA — it serves the author's reach, not the reader's job. End on an action the CMO can take Monday.
Attach an inline source to the two load-bearing stats ('$1.3 trillion,' '2.5 seconds of active attention'). One fix that also raises Gate 2 (defensibility) and Gate 3 (answer-engine citability).
Surface the reader's emotional/career job early: the CMO who bet a 2026 budget on reach and now has to answer for it. Right now only the functional job is on the page.
Front-load the one-sentence thesis so an answer engine can extract it; today it sits at paragraph 8, behind two thinkers' setups.
